ru: признавать, признать (неприятное); смотреть правде в глаза
separable: inseparable — *face up to the truth*, never *face the truth up to*; a pronoun stays outside too, *face up to it*
gloss: To accept an unpleasant fact or situation instead of avoiding it.
examples: You have to *face up to* the fact that the store is losing money.
He finally *faced up to* his drinking problem.
She is *facing up to* life without him.

separable: no object — the opponent arrives through *against*: *face off against the champion*, never *face the champion off*
gloss: To come up against an opponent in a contest or a confrontation.
examples: The two teams *face off* again in October.
The candidates *faced off* in a televised debate.
They are *facing off* against last year's champions.

ru: осаживать, осадить; давать отпор, дать отпор
separable: separable — *face down the hecklers*, and with a pronoun it must split, *face them down*
gloss: To stop or defeat someone by confronting them boldly instead of backing away.
examples: A good manager knows how to *face down* an angry customer.
She *faced* the hecklers *down* without raising her voice.
He has *faced down* tougher opponents than this.

separable: separable — *factor in the taxes*, *factor the taxes in*, and a pronoun must split it, *factor it in*
gloss: To include something in a calculation or a decision.
examples: Don't forget to *factor in* the cost of shipping.
We *factored* the delay *in* when we set the deadline.
Have you *factored in* how long the drive takes?

ru: входить в расчёт, учитываться; влиять, повлиять
separable: inseparable in this sense — *the weather factored into our decision*; what is affected always follows *into*
gloss: To be one of the things that influences a decision or a result.
examples: Salary *factors into* the choice, but it is not everything.
His age *factored into* the team's decision.
Weather is *factoring into* the delay more than anyone expected.
contrast: There is also a transitive pattern, and there the thing counted sits inside: *factor the cost into the budget*.

separable: no object — *the sound faded away*; nothing can come between the two words
gloss: To grow gradually weaker or quieter until it is gone.
examples: Old soldiers never die; they just *fade away*.
The applause *faded away* and the hall went quiet.
My memory of that year is slowly *fading away*.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *fade out the music*, *fade it out*; often there is no object at all, *the song fades out*
transitivity: both — transitive (fade out the music), intransitive (the song fades out)
gloss: To make a sound or a picture disappear gradually, or to disappear that way.
examples: The engineer *fades out* the guitar at the end.
The last scene *faded out* to black.
They are *fading* the credits *out* over the theme song.

separable: separable, and with a pronoun it must split — *fake him out*, and *fake out the defender*
gloss: To trick someone by pretending to do one thing and then doing another.
examples: He *fakes out* the goalie every single time.
The receiver *faked* the defender *out* and walked into the end zone.
Don't try *faking* me *out* — I know that trick.
contrast: American, and at home in sports above all. The noun is *a fake*: *he went in for the fake*.

separable: usually no object — *the searchers fanned out*; when it takes one it splits, *fan the cards out*
transitivity: both — intransitive (the police fanned out), transitive (fan the cards out)
gloss: To spread out from one point across a wide area.
examples: The volunteers *fan out* across the park at dawn.
Police *fanned out* through the neighborhood.
Rescue teams are *fanning out* along the riverbank.
contrast: *Fan* doubles its n before an ending: *fanned*, *fanning*.

ru: передавать, передать (работу) на сторону; отдавать на субподряд
separable: separable — *farm out the translation*, *farm the translation out*, *farm it out*
gloss: To send work to people outside your own company or household to do.
examples: Small firms often *farm out* their payroll.
The studio *farmed* the animation *out* to a shop in Vancouver.
They have been *farming out* customer service for years.

separable: separable — *fatten up the calves*, *fatten them up*
transitivity: both — transitive (fatten up the turkey), intransitive (he fattened up over the winter)
gloss: To make a person or an animal heavier by feeding them well, or to get heavier that way.
examples: Grandma is determined to *fatten* us *up*.
They *fattened up* the hogs on corn.
The puppy has *fattened up* since we got him.

separable: separable — *fence in the yard*, *fence the yard in*, and a pronoun must split it, *fence it in*
gloss: To put a fence around an area, or to make someone feel trapped by rules.
examples: We want to *fence in* the back yard for the dog.
They *fenced* the pasture *in* last spring.
He quit because he felt *fenced in* by the rules.

separable: separable — *fence off the pond*, *fence it off*
gloss: To separate one area from another with a fence or a barrier.
examples: The city will *fence off* the construction site.
They *fenced* the pool area *off* for safety.
Half the beach has been *fenced off* since the storm.

separable: separable — *fend off the questions*, *fend them off*
gloss: To push away or hold back an attack, a question, or an unwanted person.
examples: She *fends off* reporters with a smile.
He *fended* the dog *off* with his backpack.
The company has been *fending off* a takeover all year.

ru: обходиться своими силами, заботиться о себе
separable: inseparable, and the object is almost always a reflexive pronoun — *fend for yourself*, *fend for themselves*
gloss: To take care of yourself without help from anyone.
examples: At eighteen he had to *fend for* himself.
After the divorce she *fended for* herself for years.
I'm *fending for* myself this week while she travels.

separable: separable — *ferret out the truth*, *ferret it out*
gloss: To find something hidden by searching hard and patiently.
examples: A good auditor will *ferret out* every missing dollar.
She *ferreted out* the original contract in the basement.
Reporters are still *ferreting out* who paid for the trip.

separable: no object — *just fess up*; what you admit to follows *to*, *fess up to the mistake*
gloss: To admit that you did something wrong.
examples: Come on, *fess up* — who ate the last slice?
He *fessed up* to breaking the window.
Nobody is *fessing up*, so everybody stays late.
contrast: Informal and American, a clipped *confess*. In writing use *admit* or *confess*.

ru: теребить, вертеть в руках; возиться с
separable: inseparable — *fiddle with the knob*, never *fiddle the knob with*; a pronoun stays outside, *fiddle with it*
gloss: To keep touching or adjusting something, often nervously and to no purpose.
examples: Stop *fiddling with* your phone while I'm talking.
He *fiddled with* the thermostat all evening.
She *fiddles with* her ring whenever she's nervous.

separable: no object — *quit fiddling around*; what you handle follows *with*
gloss: To waste time on small unimportant things.
examples: We *fiddled around* all morning and got nothing done.
He *fiddles around* in the garage every Saturday.
Stop *fiddling around* and finish your homework.

ru: разбираться, разобраться; понимать, понять; выяснять, выяснить
separable: separable — *figure out the answer*, *figure the answer out*, and a pronoun must split it, *figure it out*
gloss: To find the answer to something by thinking about it.
examples: I can't *figure out* how to open this jar.
She *figured out* the password on the third try.
We are still *figuring out* where to park.

separable: separable, and a pronoun must split it — *figure her out*, *figure out my brother*
gloss: To come to understand what a person is really like or why they behave as they do.
examples: I've known him for years and I still can't *figure* him *out*.
She *figured* me *out* in about ten minutes.
Some people are not worth *figuring out*.

separable: inseparable — *figure on twenty guests*, never *figure twenty guests on*
gloss: To expect something or plan for it.
examples: *Figure on* an hour in traffic each way.
We *figured on* finishing by June and we were wrong.
How many people are you *figuring on*?
contrast: American and informal. British speakers say *reckon on*, or simply *expect*.

ru: учитывать, учесть; включать, включить в расчёт
separable: separable — *figure in the tip*, *figure the tip in*, *figure it in*
gloss: To include something when you work out a total.
examples: Did you *figure in* the sales tax?
He *figured* the gas money *in* before quoting a price.
Nobody *figured in* how much snow we would get.

ru: подшивать, подшить (в дело); откладывать, отложить (в памяти)
separable: separable — *file away the receipts*, *file them away*
gloss: To put a document where it belongs for storage, or to store a fact in your mind for later.
examples: Please *file away* last year's invoices.
She *filed* the compliment *away* and said nothing.
He has *filed away* every letter his father sent.

ru: подавать, подать заявление (на развод, о банкротстве)
separable: inseparable — *file for divorce*, never *file divorce for*
gloss: To apply for something officially through a court or a government office.
examples: They *filed for* bankruptcy in March.
She is *filing for* divorce after eleven years.
You have to *file for* an extension by Tuesday.

separable: separable — *fill out the form*, *fill the form out*, and a pronoun must split it, *fill it out*
gloss: To write the required information in every space on a form.
examples: Please *fill out* this form before you sit down.
I *filled* the application *out* twice.
She is *filling out* the paperwork now.
contrast: Americans *fill out* a form; the British *fill in* a form. Both are understood everywhere.

separable: no object in this sense — *he has filled out a lot*
gloss: To become fuller and less thin in the body.
examples: Boys often *fill out* at sixteen or seventeen.
He *filled out* after he started lifting.
She has *filled out* since the baby.

separable: separable — *fill in your name*, *fill your name in*, *fill it in*
gloss: To write information in the blank spaces of a form or a chart.
examples: *Fill in* your address on the second line.
He *filled in* the date and signed it.
She was *filling in* the last box when the bell rang.

ru: вводить в курс дела, ввести в курс дела
separable: separable, and the person sits inside — *fill me in*, *fill the new guy in*; the subject follows *on*, *fill me in on the details*
gloss: To tell someone the information they missed.
examples: *Fill* me *in* — what did I miss?
She *filled* us *in* on the whole argument.
He is *filling* the new guy *in* right now.

separable: inseparable — *fill in for the teacher*, never *fill the teacher in for*
gloss: To do someone else's job for a short time while they are away.
examples: Can you *fill in for* me on Friday?
A retired nurse *filled in for* her all summer.
He is *filling in for* the regular host this week.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *fill up the tank*, *fill it up*; often intransitive, *the theater filled up*
transitivity: both — transitive (fill up the tank), intransitive (the lot filled up fast)
gloss: To make something completely full, or to become completely full.
examples: *Fill* it *up* with regular, please.
The parking lot *filled up* by nine.
We are *filling up* the water jugs before the storm.

separable: inseparable after *up* — *fill up on bread*; the eater is the subject, not an object
gloss: To eat so much of one thing that you have no room left for anything else.
examples: Don't *fill up on* chips before dinner.
The kids *filled up on* popcorn at the movie.
He is *filling up on* free bread again.

separable: separable — *filter out the spam*, *filter it out*
gloss: To remove unwanted things from a group or a flow and keep the rest.
examples: The software *filters out* most junk mail.
They *filtered out* every application without a degree.
These glasses are *filtering out* the blue light.

separable: no object — *the news filtered through*; who it reaches follows *to*
gloss: Of news or information, to spread slowly from person to person.
examples: Word *filters through* the office within an hour.
The results *filtered through* to us late that night.
Details are still *filtering through*.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *finish up the report*, *finish it up*; also used alone, *we finished up around six*
transitivity: both — transitive (finish up your homework), intransitive (we finished up late)
gloss: To complete the last part of something.
examples: Let me *finish up* this email and I'll come.
They *finished up* the kitchen on Saturday.
She is *finishing up* her last semester.

ru: доедать, доесть; допивать, допить; приканчивать, прикончить
separable: separable — *finish off the pizza*, *finish it off*
gloss: To eat, drink, or use the last of something.
examples: Who *finished off* the coffee?
He *finishes off* a gallon of milk a week.
We are *finishing off* the leftovers tonight.

separable: separable, and with a pronoun it must split — *finish him off*, and *finish off the wounded animal*
gloss: To destroy or defeat someone or something completely, or to be the final blow.
examples: Two more losses would *finish off* their season.
The flood *finished off* what was left of the crop.
That last hill nearly *finished* me *off*.

separable: separable — *fire up the grill*, *fire it up*
gloss: To start a machine, an engine, or a program.
examples: *Fire up* the grill — they'll be here at six.
He *fired up* the old tractor on the first try.
She is *firing up* her laptop now.

separable: separable — *fire up the crowd*, *fire them up*; very common in the passive, *I'm fired up*
gloss: To fill someone with energy and enthusiasm.
examples: Her speech *fires up* the volunteers every year.
The coach *fired* the team *up* at halftime.
Everyone is *fired up* about the new season.

separable: separable — *fire off an email*, *fire it off*
gloss: To send a message quickly, usually in anger or in haste.
examples: She *fires off* a dozen texts before breakfast.
He *fired off* an angry letter to the landlord.
I'm *firing off* a quick note to the team.

separable: no object — almost always the bare imperative, *fire away*
gloss: To go ahead and ask your questions or say what you came to say.
examples: You have three questions? *Fire away*.
He said *fire away*, so I asked about the money.
The reporters *fired away* for a full hour.

separable: no object — the reply arrives through *with*, *fired back with numbers*
gloss: To answer a criticism quickly and sharply.
examples: Critics complained, and the studio *fired back*.
She *fired back* with numbers of her own.
He is *firing back* at every post about him.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *firm up the dates*, *firm them up*; intransitive of things that set, *the dough firms up*
transitivity: both — transitive (firm up the details), intransitive (the sauce firms up as it cools)
gloss: To make plans or details more definite, or to become more solid.
examples: Let's *firm up* the schedule by Friday.
They *firmed up* the offer in writing.
The dough is *firming up* in the fridge.

separable: separable — *fish out the keys*, *fish them out*
gloss: To pull something out of a bag, a pocket, or water after searching for it.
examples: He *fishes out* a coin and hands it to her.
She *fished* her phone *out* of the couch.
They are *fishing* branches *out* of the pool.

separable: inseparable — *fish for compliments*, never *fish compliments for*
gloss: To try to get something indirectly, without asking for it openly.
examples: He's *fishing for* a compliment and you know it.
She *fished for* details about the promotion.
Reporters were *fishing for* a quote all afternoon.

ru: приводить в порядок, привести в порядок; ремонтировать, отремонтировать
separable: separable — *fix up the house*, *fix it up*
gloss: To repair or improve something that is old or in bad condition.
examples: They bought a wreck and *fixed* it *up*.
He *fixes up* old bikes and gives them away.
We have been *fixing up* the basement all winter.

ru: сводить, свести (кого-л. с кем-л.); устраивать, устроить
separable: separable, and the person sits inside — *fix me up with her cousin*, *fix them up with a room*
gloss: To arrange for someone to meet a romantic partner, or to provide someone with what they need.
examples: My sister wants to *fix* me *up* with her coworker.
They *fixed* us *up* with two tickets and a hotel.
He keeps *fixing* people *up*, and it never works.
contrast: The noun from the romantic sense is *a setup* or *a blind date*; *a fixer-upper* is a house that needs work.

ru: сходить на нет, сойти на нет; выдыхаться, выдохнуться
separable: no object — *the protest fizzled out*
gloss: To end weakly after a promising start.
examples: Most New Year's resolutions *fizzle out* by February.
The storm *fizzled out* before it reached the coast.
Their romance is *fizzling out*.

separable: separable — *flag down a cab*, and with a pronoun it must split, *flag him down*
gloss: To signal a driver to stop by waving.
examples: You'll never *flag down* a cab in this rain.
She *flagged* a passing truck *down*.
He is out on the corner *flagging down* a ride.
contrast: *Flag* doubles its g before an ending: *flagged*, *flagging*.

separable: no object — the person you let down follows *on*, *flaked out on us*
gloss: To fail to do what you promised, especially by not showing up.
examples: He *flakes out* on plans about half the time.
Two people *flaked out* an hour before the party.
She's *flaking out* on us again.
contrast: Informal American. Someone who does this habitually is *a flake*.

separable: no object — the person you turn on follows *at*, *he flared up at me*
gloss: To suddenly become very angry.
examples: He *flares up* whenever money comes up.
She *flared up* at the waiter over nothing.
Tempers are *flaring up* in the comments.

separable: no object — *her arthritis flared up*
gloss: Of an illness, a pain, or a conflict, to become severe again after a quiet period.
examples: My knee *flares up* in cold weather.
Fighting *flared up* along the border last night.
Her eczema has *flared up* again.
contrast: The noun is one word: *a flare-up of the old injury*.

separable: no object — what you remember follows *to*, *flashed back to that night*
gloss: To suddenly remember a past scene as if you were living it again.
examples: Every siren makes him *flash back* to the crash.
She *flashed back* to her first day of school.
I keep *flashing back* to that conversation.
contrast: The noun is one word: *a flashback*.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *flatten out the dough*, *flatten it out*; intransitive of roads and curves, *the trail flattens out*
transitivity: both — transitive (flatten out the map), intransitive (the road flattens out)
gloss: To become level, or to make something level.
examples: The climb *flattens out* after the second mile.
Sales *flattened out* in the fall.
He is *flattening* the dough *out* with a rolling pin.

separable: separable — *flesh out the proposal*, *flesh it out*
gloss: To add detail to an idea, a plan, or a story that is still only an outline.
examples: Can you *flesh out* the middle section?
She *fleshed out* the outline over the weekend.
The character is still being *fleshed out*.

ru: выходить из себя, выйти из себя; психовать, психануть
separable: no object — *my dad flipped out*; what set you off follows *over* or *about*
gloss: To lose control of yourself from anger, shock, or excitement.
examples: My mom is going to *flip out* when she sees this.
He *flipped out* over a parking spot.
Half the office is *flipping out* about the new policy.
contrast: *Flip* doubles its p before an ending: *flipped*, *flipping*.

separable: inseparable — *flip through the magazine*, *flip through it*, never *flip it through*
gloss: To turn the pages of something quickly without reading carefully.
examples: He *flips through* the menu and orders the same thing.
She *flipped through* the album twice.
I was *flipping through* an old notebook and found this.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *flip over the card*, *flip it over*; intransitive of things that turn, *the kayak flipped over*
transitivity: both — transitive (flip the burger over), intransitive (the truck flipped over)
gloss: To turn something onto its other side, or to turn over.
examples: *Flip* the card *over* and read the back.
The canoe *flipped over* in the rapids.
He is *flipping over* the mattress.

separable: separable, and with a pronoun it must split — *flipped him off*, and *flip off the referee*
gloss: To make a rude gesture at someone with the middle finger.
examples: Some guy *flipped* me *off* on the freeway.
Don't *flip off* the referee — you'll be ejected.
He got a ticket for *flipping off* a cop.
contrast: Rude and very informal, but everywhere in speech. The gesture itself is *the finger*: *he gave me the finger*.

separable: no object — *a rumor is floating around*
gloss: Of a rumor, an idea, or a mislaid object, to be circulating or lying somewhere unnoticed.
examples: A story like that *floats around* for years.
That name *floated around* the office all week.
There's a spare key *floating around* here somewhere.

ru: хлынуть потоком, поступать в огромном количестве
separable: no object — *donations flooded in*
gloss: To arrive in very large numbers all at once.
examples: Orders *flood in* every December.
Messages *flooded in* after the broadcast.
Applications are still *flooding in*.

separable: no object — the school follows *of*, *flunked out of college*
gloss: To be made to leave a school or a college because your grades are too low.
examples: Half the class will *flunk out* by spring.
He *flunked out* of state school after one year.
She is worried about *flunking out*.
contrast: American and informal. *Flunk* on its own means to fail a test or a course: *I flunked chemistry*.

separable: separable — *flush out the suspects*, *flush them out*
gloss: To force a person or an animal out of a hiding place.
examples: The dogs *flush out* birds for the hunters.
Police *flushed* him *out* of a motel in Reno.
They are *flushing out* whoever leaked the memo.
contrast: Not *flesh out*, which is to add detail. The two are often confused in writing.

separable: separable — *fold up the chairs*, *fold them up*; also intransitive of furniture, *the table folds up*
transitivity: both — transitive (fold up the map), intransitive (the stroller folds up)
gloss: To bend something over on itself so that it takes up less room.
examples: *Fold up* the blanket and put it in the trunk.
He *folded* the letter *up* and slid it into his pocket.
This crib *folds up* in about ten seconds.

separable: separable — *fold in the egg whites*, *fold them in*
gloss: To mix an ingredient into a batter gently, turning it over rather than stirring hard.
examples: *Fold in* the chocolate chips at the very end.
She *folded* the whipped cream *in* a spoonful at a time.
Keep *folding in* the flour until it disappears.

ru: напоминать о себе, связываться повторно; принимать дальнейшие меры
separable: usually no object — *I'll follow up tomorrow*; the person follows *with*, the matter follows *on*
gloss: To take further action after a first contact or a first step.
examples: I'll *follow up* with the client on Monday.
She *followed up* by email the next day.
Nobody is *following up*, so nothing gets done.
contrast: The noun is hyphenated: *a follow-up call*, *send a follow-up*.

ru: проверять, проверить (что стало с чем-л.); доводить до конца
separable: inseparable — *follow up on the complaint*, never *follow the complaint up on*
gloss: To check on something started earlier, or to act on information you were given.
examples: Did anyone *follow up on* that lead?
She *followed up on* every name in the file.
We are *following up on* last week's estimate.

ru: доводить до конца, довести до конца (обещанное)
separable: no object — what you promised follows *on*, *follow through on the plan*
gloss: To finish what you said you would do instead of stopping halfway.
examples: He makes big promises but never *follows through*.
They *followed through* on every repair they listed.
*Following through* is the hard part.

ru: следить (за объяснением), не отставать; повторять за
separable: no object — what you keep up with follows *with*, *follow along with the recording*
gloss: To keep up with something as it is being read, shown, or played.
examples: *Follow along* in your book while I read.
The kids *followed along* with the video.
He is *following along* on his own guitar.

separable: separable, and a pronoun must split it — *follows me around*, and *follow the guide around*
gloss: To go everywhere someone goes, usually to their annoyance.
examples: The puppy *follows* her *around* all day.
He *followed* me *around* the store asking questions.
Stop *following* your brother *around*.

separable: no object — *quit fooling around*
gloss: To behave in a silly way or waste time instead of working.
examples: Quit *fooling around* and get in the car.
They *fooled around* on the ice for an hour.
He *fools around* in class and then asks me for help.

separable: inseparable — *fool around with the wiring*, never *fool the wiring around with*
gloss: To handle or experiment with something you would be wiser to leave alone.
examples: Don't *fool around with* the gas line yourself.
He *fooled around with* the settings and broke it.
She has been *fooling around with* a new recipe.

separable: inseparable — *fooling around with his coworker*
gloss: To have a casual sexual relationship with someone, often while committed to someone else.
examples: Everyone knew he was *fooling around with* someone at work.
She *fooled around with* him one summer and that was it.
If he *fools around with* her, that marriage is over.
contrast: Informal. Without *with*, *fool around* can carry the same meaning: *they were fooling around in the back seat*.

separable: separable — *force out the manager*, *force him out*; very common in the passive, *he was forced out*
gloss: To make someone leave a job or a position against their will.
examples: The board wants to *force out* the founder.
They *forced* her *out* after twenty years.
Two directors have been *forced out* this year.

ru: впихивать в себя, съедать через силу; глотать через силу
separable: separable — *force down the medicine*, *force it down*
gloss: To make yourself swallow food or drink you do not want.
examples: I *forced down* two bites to be polite.
He *forces down* a protein shake every morning.
She is *forcing down* the last of the soup.

separable: separable — *force back the tears*, *force them back*
gloss: To hold in a strong feeling so that it does not show.
examples: She *forced back* tears through the whole speech.
He *forces back* a laugh every time they say it.
*Forcing back* a yawn, he asked another question.

separable: the thing sits inside and the person follows *on* — *force your opinions on people*, *force it on them*
gloss: To make someone accept something they do not want.
examples: Nobody is *forcing* this *on* you.
He *forced* his taste in music *on* the whole car.
Rules *forced on* a team from outside rarely stick.
contrast: *Force upon* is the same verb, a shade more formal.

separable: no object — what you press on with follows *with*, *forge ahead with the plan*
gloss: To keep moving forward with determination in spite of difficulty.
examples: The city is *forging ahead* with the bridge project.
They *forged ahead* even after the funding fell through.
He *forges ahead* while everyone else is still arguing.

separable: separable — *fork over the money*, *fork it over*
gloss: To hand over money, usually unwillingly.
examples: *Fork* it *over* — you lost the bet.
We *forked over* four hundred dollars for the repair.
Fans are *forking over* a fortune for these seats.
contrast: *Fork out* and *fork up* mean the same thing; *fork over* is the most American of the three.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *foul up the schedule*, *foul it up*; also used alone, *I fouled up*
transitivity: both — transitive (foul up the order), intransitive (the new guy fouled up)
gloss: To spoil something by doing it badly or by making a mistake.
examples: One bad form can *foul up* the whole application.
The airline *fouled up* our reservation.
He is *fouling up* the numbers again.
contrast: The noun is one word: *a foul-up at the front desk*.

separable: no object — *he fouled out in the fourth quarter*
gloss: In basketball, to be sent off the court for committing too many fouls.
examples: Their center *fouls out* almost every game.
He *fouled out* with four minutes left.
Two starters have *fouled out*.

separable: separable — *free up some space*, *free it up*
gloss: To make time, money, space, or a person available for something else.
examples: Deleting those videos will *free up* a lot of space.
The grant *freed up* money for new hires.
Moving the meeting is *freeing up* my whole afternoon.
contrast: *Free* keeps both e's: *freed*, *freeing* — never *freing*.

separable: no object in this sense — *don't freak out*; what upset you follows *about* or *over*
gloss: To become suddenly very frightened, upset, or excited.
examples: Don't *freak out*, but the car is making that noise again.
She *freaked out* when she saw the bill.
I'm *freaking out* about the interview.

separable: separable, and with a pronoun it must split — *that movie freaked me out*
gloss: To frighten or deeply unsettle someone.
examples: Clowns *freak* my sister *out*.
The noise in the attic *freaked* us *out*.
Stop *freaking* people *out* with those stories.

ru: освежаться, освежиться; приводить себя в порядок
separable: usually no object — *I'd like to freshen up*; transitive with a room or a drink, and then it splits, *freshen it up*
transitivity: both — intransitive (let me freshen up), transitive (freshen up the guest room)
gloss: To wash and tidy yourself, or to make something look or taste new again.
examples: Let me *freshen up* before we go.
She *freshened up* in the airport bathroom.
He is *freshening up* the paint in the hallway.

separable: separable — *frighten off the deer*, *frighten them off*
gloss: To scare a person or an animal so that they go away or give up.
examples: A porch light will *frighten off* most raccoons.
High prices *frightened off* the buyers.
The dog has *frightened off* two delivery drivers.
contrast: *Frighten away* is the same verb with the same meaning and the same separability.

separable: separable — *fritter away the money*, *fritter it away*
gloss: To waste time or money little by little on unimportant things.
examples: Don't *fritter away* the whole weekend on your phone.
He *frittered away* his inheritance in three years.
She is *frittering away* the best years of her career.

separable: inseparable — *front for the syndicate*, never *front the syndicate for*
gloss: To act publicly as a cover for a person or an organization doing something secret.
examples: The car wash *fronts for* a money-laundering operation.
He *fronted for* investors who wanted to stay anonymous.
Two shell companies were *fronting for* the same man.

separable: inseparable — *frown on tattoos*, never *frown tattoos on*; most often passive, *it is frowned on here*
gloss: To disapprove of something, especially as a matter of custom or policy.
examples: The company *frowns on* dating between managers and staff.
Her family *frowned on* the marriage.
Showing up late is *frowned on* around here.
contrast: *Frown upon* is the same verb, a shade more formal: *such behavior is frowned upon*.

separable: usually no object — *we fueled up in Reno*; transitive with the vehicle, and then it splits, *fuel it up*
transitivity: both — intransitive (let's fuel up first), transitive (fuel up the plane)
gloss: To fill a vehicle with gas, or to eat well before a long effort.
examples: Let's *fuel up* before we hit the desert.
They *fueled up* on pancakes and left at six.
The jet is *fueling up* now.
contrast: American spelling keeps one l: *fueled*, *fueling*. British writing doubles it: *fuelled*, *fuelling*.

ru: носиться с, хлопотать над; суетиться вокруг
separable: inseparable — *fuss over the baby*, never *fuss the baby over*
gloss: To give someone or something far more attention and care than is needed.
examples: Grandma *fusses over* every guest who walks in.
He *fussed over* the seating chart for a week.
Stop *fussing over* me — I'm fine.

separable: inseparable — *fuss with her hair*, never *fuss her hair with*
gloss: To keep touching or adjusting something in a restless way.
examples: He *fusses with* his tie whenever he's nervous.
She *fussed with* the flowers until they were perfect.
Quit *fussing with* the antenna and sit down.
